license_interpretation: SANA-Sprint weights are Apache-2.0. The bundled Gemma 2 text encoder is under the Gemma Terms of Use (https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms) and the Gemma Prohibited Use Policy. Apache-2.0 is a permissive license, so the SANA-Sprint transformer and autoencoder can be used in commercial and closed-source products; it asks you to keep its license text and attribution notices with any copy you redistribute, and it grants a patent license. NVIDIA declares it on the Hugging Face repository LibreYOLO downloads, Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_Sprint_0.6B_1024px_diffusers, in its license tag and LICENSE file, and the model card names the Gemma terms for Gemma-2-2B-IT alongside it. The Gemma Terms of Use are Google's own agreement, not an OSI-approved license: redistributing the encoder means passing the Prohibited Use Policy's restrictions on to your users as an enforceable provision, with a copy of the terms. LibreYOLO's loader prints the notice above the first time it loads the model in a session. Read both documents before shipping a product on this model. LibreYOLO's adapter is its own MIT code that calls the Apache-2.0 diffusers SanaSprintPipeline; no upstream source is ported. The weights are not redistributed: they download from that repository at revision aa76e7f4f4928f378716b6716a2130fba3caf5b1.
